artifacts.summary: Root-cause confirmation, sibling-hook fix pattern, full hook-idiom survey (52 sites, 1 defect), and resolved design questions for the malformed-marker diagnosability defect.

memory_candidates.content: In bash+jq hooks, `jq -r '.field // "non-empty default"' FILE 2>/dev/null` silently drops the default and yields empty string when FILE fails to parse as JSON at all -- the `//` alternative operator only fires on `null`/`false` results, never on a parse error, and `2>/dev/null` hides jq's own diagnostic. Guard with `jq empty FILE 2>/dev/null || <handle-parse-failure>` before the extraction whenever the fallback is a meaningful non-empty value. When the fallback is `// empty` (or another effectively-empty value the caller already treats as no-op), the distinction is usually safe to leave unguarded since parse-error and missing-field collapse to the same caller behavior.

When a hook needs to correlate an event to a session_id but its primary content source (e.g. a marker file) fails to parse, a task/session identifier can often still be recovered from the file's PATH (e.g. a `specs/{N}_{slug}/` directory segment) even when its CONTENT is unusable, then resolved to session_id via a specs/state.json `.active_projects[] | select(.project_number == $num) | .session_id` lookup. This is the same fallback events-log-lifecycle.sh's Stop path already uses when its own primary source lacks session_id directly -- reusable whenever a correlation ID needs a path-based escape hatch around a content-parsing failure.
